title: Copilot Notebooks: Power BI reports as references
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned Notebook capability from documented Copilot Chat behaviour and existing administrative controls. The Graph automation note needs a small clarification: applying the policy requires applyOnce mode, rather than the default monitoring-only mode.

claims.quote: Copilot Notebooks now lets users add Power BI reports as references, bringing report data directly into their notebooks alongside files.

claims.claim: Copilot uses the report information to help generate grounded summaries, presentations and briefs.
claims.quote: Copilot uses this information to help generate more relevant summaries, presentations, and briefs grounded in the organization's data.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe Power BI reports as Copilot Notebook references.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" "Power BI" references license admin default permissions; "Notebooks" "Power BI reports"; site:learn.microsoft.com "569928". Opened Copilot Power BI, Fabric IQ, and Notebooks admin, requirements and permissions pages; none describes this capability.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The arrival default for Power BI references in Notebooks is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" "Power BI" references license admin default permissions; "Copilot Notebooks" references administrator enable Power BI Graph. Read roadmap, Notebooks admin policies and Copilot Power BI settings; no default for the new reference type is stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot already grounds chat responses in Power BI reports, including specifically shared reports.
claims.quote: Copilot will ground responses in Power BI data, including scenarios where users share a specific report and scenarios where Copilot finds the right report automatically.

claims.claim: The existing Microsoft Copilot Power BI answering capability and its Microsoft 365 setting are enabled by default.
claims.quote: Fabric data available in M365 Copilot: This setting controls whether Fabric data appears in Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences. The setting is enabled by default.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot Notebooks can be shared with colleagues.
claims.quote: Copilot Notebooks can be shared.

claims.claim: For Copilot Chat, Power BI data is accessed using the user's existing permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot uses the user's existing permissions, including row-level security (RLS) and object-level security (OLS), to access the data.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat respects row-level security on the underlying Power BI semantic model.
claims.quote: Copilot respects RLS and OLS applied to the underlying semantic model. Answers only reflect the data the user has permission to see.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat respects object-level security on the underlying Power BI semantic model.
claims.quote: Copilot respects RLS and OLS applied to the underlying semantic model. Answers only reflect the data the user has permission to see.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described whose Power BI permissions determine the report-derived content available to Notebook collaborators.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" "Power BI" references license admin default permissions; "Copilot Notebooks" "Power BI" sensitivity labels sharing billing. Opened Notebooks permissions and Fabric IQ: private chats and file sharing are described, but not Power BI reference authorisation for collaborators.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not establish whether the two existing Power BI integration settings govern the new Notebook reference type.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" references administrator enable Power BI Graph; "Copilot Notebooks" "Power BI" references license admin default permissions. Opened Copilot Power BI, Fabric IQ and metadata-sharing pages; their documented experiences do not identify Notebook references.

claims.claim: Fabric metadata sharing is on by default when the Fabric and Microsoft 365 tenants are in the same geographic region.
claims.quote: The setting is turned on by default when your Fabric tenant and Microsoft 365 tenant are in the same geographic region.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks Cloud Policy governs Notebook creation and access through the Copilot app.
claims.quote: When creation is disabled, users are unable to create new Copilot Pages or Notebooks. The Pages module is visible in the Microsoft Copilot app, but the Notebooks module is hidden, preventing users from accessing existing Notebooks through the Copilot App.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling the Cloud Policy prevents new Notebook creation for users in scope.
claims.quote: When creation is disabled, users are unable to create new Copilot Pages or Notebooks.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling the Cloud Policy hides the Notebooks module in the Copilot app.
claims.quote: The Pages module is visible in the Microsoft Copilot app, but the Notebooks module is hidden, preventing users from accessing existing Notebooks through the Copilot App.

claims.claim: Disabling creation does not delete existing items.
claims.quote: Existing Copilot Pages and Notebooks aren't deleted.

claims.claim: Users with permission can still view and edit existing items through the access routes documented by Microsoft.
claims.quote: Users can still view and edit existing items if they have permission. These files remain accessible in the following ways:

claims.claim: Files added to Notebooks remain available in their OneDrive and SharePoint storage locations.
claims.quote: Original storage locations: Files added to Notebooks remain available in OneDrive and SharePoint where they're stored

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center path is Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.
claims.quote: Select Customization from the left pane. ... Select Policy Management. ... Create a new policy configuration or edit an existing one. ... From the Choose the scope dropdown list ... In Configure Settings ... Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply the Notebook Cloud Policy through the named copilotpagesnotebooks resource and its value property.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor object that runs periodically in the background at a scheduled frequency to detect configuration drift in monitorOnly mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[0].note: 'Set mode to applyOnce to apply the policy; the default monitorOnly mode only detects drift. The baseline resource is microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks, with properties.value set to the string "0" or "1".' The mode is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta and the resource at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-copilot-resources.

claims.claim: The beta TCM automation supports these Cloud Policy settings only at tenant level.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: applyOnce fails for the resource if a group-level policy configures the target setting.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: The resource is microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks and its value property accepts 0 or 1.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks" ... "properties": { "value": "1" } ... 0 disables the setting; 1 enables the setting.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Fabric data access is configured in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > Fabric data in Microsoft Copilot > Step 1.
claims.quote: select Copilot > Settings. ... select View all. ... Select Fabric data in Microsoft Copilot. ... Under Step 1, choose which users can access Fabric data in Microsoft Copilot

claims.claim: The Fabric data access setting offers No users, All users and Specific groups.
claims.quote: Under Step 1, choose which users can access Fabric data in Microsoft Copilot: No users, All users, or Specific groups.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the Microsoft 365 admin center Fabric data access setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Fabric data" "Copilot" Microsoft Graph PowerShell setting API; "Fabric data in Microsoft Copilot" "Graph" API; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "Fabric" "Copilot" settings. Read Copilot Power BI and TCM Copilot resources; no operation for this setting.

claims.claim: The cited Power BI integration pages do not name Copilot Notebooks.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" references administrator enable Power BI Graph. Read Use Power BI data in Microsoft Copilot, Fabric IQ in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Share data with your Microsoft 365 services in full; none names Copilot Notebooks.

claims.claim: In Microsoft Fabric, metadata sharing is at OneLake catalog > Govern > Configurations > Tenant settings > Share Fabric data with your Microsoft 365 services.
claims.quote: Go to OneLake catalog > Govern > Configurations > Tenant settings > Share Fabric data with your Microsoft 365 services.

claims.claim: POST https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/admin/tenantsettings/{tenantSettingName}/update updates a Fabric tenant setting.
claims.quote: Update a given tenant setting. ... POST https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/admin/tenantsettings/{tenantSettingName}/update

claims.claim: The Fabric update operation uses the enabled request-body property to enable or disable the setting.
claims.quote: enabled | True | boolean | The status of the tenant setting. False - Disabled, True - Enabled.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A Fabric administrator configures the Fabric metadata-sharing setting.
claims.quote: a Fabric administrator will need to enable the Share data with your Microsoft 365 services tenant setting in the Fabric admin portal.

claims.claim: Shared Fabric metadata feeds Copilot search and report attachment menus.
claims.quote: The shared metadata enables Power BI content to appear in Copilot search and the item-attachment menu.

claims.claim: Turning off Fabric metadata sharing does not block all Fabric content from appearing in Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Turning off this setting doesn't block Fabric content from appearing in Microsoft 365. Users who have access to Fabric content can still take explicit action to use that content in Microsoft 365 products.

claims.claim: When metadata sharing is off, Copilot Chat users can still explicitly paste report links or name reports.
claims.quote: When this setting is off, users can still paste report links or name reports in their prompts.

claims.claim: Fabric metadata-sharing setting changes can take up to 24 hours.
claims.quote: Changes can take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.claim: By default, Fabric shares information only within the geography of the Fabric tenant.
claims.quote: By default, Fabric only shares information within the geography where your Fabric tenant is located.

claims.claim: A second toggle permits sharing when Fabric and Microsoft 365 tenants are in different geographies.
claims.quote: If your Microsoft 365 tenant is in a different geography, you need to allow cross-geography sharing for the integration to work. You can enable cross-geography sharing by using a second toggle in the tenant setting.

claims.claim: When Copilot users retrieve Fabric data, their Copilot query data is shared with Fabric.
claims.quote: When you allow Microsoft Copilot users to search and retrieve data stored in Fabric, their query data from Microsoft Copilot will be shared with Fabric.

claims.claim: Data processed in Fabric is subject to Fabric Product Terms.
claims.quote: Fabric operates separately from Microsoft Copilot and has different commitments. Data processed in Fabric is subject to Fabric Product Terms.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Copilot Chat honours Power BI sensitivity labels and generated content inherits the conversation's sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Copilot honors the sensitivity labels applied to Power BI reports and semantic models used in a conversation. ... Content that you create from the conversation, such as an exported spreadsheet, inherits the conversation's sensitivity label.

claims.claim: DLP policies apply to Power BI content in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Data loss prevention (DLP) policies also apply. If a DLP policy prohibits Copilot from processing content with a specific sensitivity label, Copilot doesn't use Power BI content with that label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how Power BI reference labels and protections carry into Notebook content.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" "Power BI" sensitivity labels sharing billing. Read Fabric IQ sensitivity labels, Notebooks permissions and Notebooks compliance-summary search excerpt; general Notebook DLP is documented, but Power BI reference label propagation is not.

claims.claim: For Copilot Chat, Power BI answers reflect the semantic model's last refresh rather than real-time data.
claims.quote: Answers reflect the data from the last refresh of the semantic model, not real-time data. Answers are only as current as the most recent successful refresh.
